chapter_title: The Group Assembled and Reality Fractured
summary: Runciter finally assembles the complete group of eleven inertials for the Luna mission. The chapter focuses on Tippy Jackson, an anti-telepath, who receives a mysterious call from Runciter summoning her to join the team. Her artificially induced EREM sleep is interrupted by a vivid dream featuring two brothers—a telepath and a precog named Matt and Bill—who speak Shakespearean verse about their deformity. When she wakes, she's unsettled by remembering poetry she doesn't recall reading. The chapter then returns to Runciter's office where he reviews each inertial: Edie Dorn, Al Hammond, Tippy Jackson, Jon Ild, Francesca Spanish, Tito Apostos, Don Denny, Sammy Mundo, Wendy Wright, and Fred Zafsky. As they gather, Pat's influence becomes apparent. Some retain fragmented memories of the altered timeline; others like Francesca Spanish report experiencing alternative worlds. The chapter ends with Joe recognizing the profound danger the group faces, despite their assembled power.

themes: Prophecy and premonition—the power of dreams to anticipate reality
The adequacy of preparedness in the face of overwhelming odds
Physical appearance and social composition (the 'ill-assorted bunch')
The burden of knowledge that preparation is insufficient

theological_concepts.context: Tippy's dream of Matt and Bill functions as premonition/warning; the poetry emerges from external source (possible telepath)
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Biblical tradition of dreams as vehicles of divine communication (Joseph, Jacob, Daniel); shamanic vision quests

theological_concepts.context: Francesca Spanish's report of inhabiting alternative world and being restored to 'rightful universe'; suggests cosmology with multiple ontological planes
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Gnostic cosmology of multiple aeons; Platonic theory of forms; Hindu Maya (illusion)

theological_concepts.context: Francesca's perception of 'vast, all-encompassing spiritual agency' restoring them suggests divine or demonic intervention
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Theology of grace; demonology; occult intervention narratives

philosophical_concepts.concept: Epistemology: How do we know what's real when multiple characters report different memories and experiences?
Metaethics: Are characters responsible for actions they don't remember committing in original timelines?
Aesthetics of the body: Why does Dick spend so much time describing characters' physical appearance and grotesqueness?
Political philosophy: What does it mean that the group is deliberately assembled by those in power, yet contains the seeds of rebellion (Pat)?
Metaphysics of time: Multiple timeline awareness suggests B-theory of time (all moments equally real); questions whether past can truly change
Psychology: Artificial EREM sleep, partial memories, and shared delusions raise questions about consciousness and mental health

key_events.event: Tippy Jackson's prophetic dream of Matt and Bill
key_events.significance: Introduces the possibility that Hollis operatives are coordinated and aware of the Runciter team; suggests extrasensory communication across organizations

key_events.event: Runciter's summons calling Tippy to service
key_events.significance: Activates the final assembly; brings the last piece into place

key_events.event: The complete assembly of eleven inertials
key_events.significance: Represents the culmination of planning and preparation; forms the core group for the lunar mission; establishes cast for the novel's main action

key_events.event: Francesca Spanish's testimony about experiencing alternative worlds
key_events.significance: Provides external confirmation of Pat's reality-altering powers; spreads awareness that something is fundamentally wrong with reality

key_events.event: Joe Chip's realization that the group is inadequate
key_events.significance: Establishes dramatic irony: despite all preparation, the team knows they will fail; suggests either prescience or deeper structural knowledge
